title: Cascaded Flow Matching for Heterogeneous Tabular Data with Mixed-Type Features
summary: Targets features that mix a discrete state with an otherwise continuous distribution, such as inflated zeros or missing codes, by generating a coarse categorical sketch of the row first and then conditioning a high-resolution flow-matching model on it through a guided probability path and data-dependent coupling, with a proof that the cascade tightens the transport-cost bound. SDV supplies both sides of the evaluation: CTGAN version 0.11.0 from the sdv-dev repository and TVAE are run as baselines, and the Shape and Trend scores that carry the fidelity results come from SDMetrics version 0.22.0.
evidence: section 5.1 names CTGAN and TVAE (Xu et al. 2019) among the baselines alongside ARF, TabDDPM, TabSyn, TabDiff and CDTD, and the results table reports their detection, shape and trend scores across twelve datasets; the implementation appendix records CTGAN as available as part of the Synthetic Data Vault at https://github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN under the Business Source License 1.1, at package version 0.11.0, with architecture dimensions adjusted to match the diffusion models' MLP; the evaluation-metrics appendix states that univariate density is measured mainly with the Shape metric from the SDMetrics library version 0.22.0 of the Synthetic Data Vault, and that bivariate density uses the Trend score from the same library

title: SemaPop: Semantic-Persona Conditioned and Controllable Population Synthesis
summary: Conditions population synthesis on semantics rather than leaving it unconditional: persona descriptions are written from survey records by a language model, encoded into a semantic space, and used as the conditioning signal for generation, which lets a planner steer the synthetic population toward a scenario instead of only reproducing the observed marginals. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the compared generators, set against Bayesian networks, a copula-based Bayesian network, TabDDPM and WGAN-GP on precision, recall and F1 over attribute combinations.
evidence: the baselines section describes CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) as a conditional GAN for tabular data employing mode-specific normalisation and conditional sampling to handle mixed discrete-continuous variables and imbalanced categorical distributions, and lists TVAE alongside TabDDPM, BN, BN-Copula and WGAN-GP; the results discussion reports CTGAN at 3.83 per cent precision against recall in the 70 to 92 per cent range, grouping it with the models that cover observed attribute combinations while generating many infeasible ones, with F1 below 32 per cent

title: Synthesizing the Counterfactual: A CTGAN-Augmented Causal Evaluation of Palliative Care on Spousal Depression
summary: Estimates whether palliative care buffers a surviving spouse against depression, a question that SHARE panel data cannot answer directly because the treated cohort is too small after attrition, by augmenting both arms with synthetic longitudinal trajectories and then applying a matched difference-in-differences estimator. CTGAN is the generator that augmentation runs on, selected over TVAE and a transformer VAE and used unmodified inside a purpose-built pipeline that flattens each survivor's waves into one wide vector, resamples a real baseline skeleton for every synthetic unit and conditions the trajectory on it, so the paper's causal estimates rest on CTGAN output.
evidence: the introduction states that a Conditional Tabular GAN (Xu et al. 2019) is employed to synthetically augment the underrepresented treated and control cohorts and that CTGAN is repurposed from a privacy tool into a statistical technique for structural data augmentation in causal designs; section 3.2 benchmarks CTGAN against TVAE (Xu et al. 2019) and a transformer-based tabular VAE using the FEST evaluation framework, then describes the adaptation as a data-processing pipeline around the model rather than a change to it: long-to-wide reshaping centred on the decedent's death, padding for staggered attrition, a Skeleton Injection partial-synthesis step that resamples a real baseline vector per synthetic unit, and post-generation clamping of clinical scores; the same section credits CTGAN's mode-specific normalisation for representing complex continuous variables without mode collapse; 3220 synthetic units are generated per treatment arm

title: Self-Improving Tabular Language Models via Iterative Reward-Guided Post-Training
summary: Treats a tabular language model as something to keep improving after supervised fine-tuning, running a generate-score-align loop in which sampled rows are ranked by a task-specified reward and the model is updated against a frozen reference, with TabGRAA comparing high- and low-reward groups by group-averaged log-ratios instead of paired preferences. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE baselines run from their official codebases, and the classifier two-sample test that scores indistinguishability is SDMetrics' C2ST quality score.
evidence: the baselines appendix lists CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) as a GAN designed for mixed-type tabular data and TVAE (Xu et al. 2019) as a VAE for tabular generation among the GAN/VAE models, and states that CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM, TabSyn and TabDiff are implemented using their official codebases and tuned following their original papers; the evaluation-metrics section says the classifier two-sample test reports the SDMetrics C2ST quality score under the SDMetrics convention, and the C2ST table reports 100 times that score for CTGAN and TVAE against the diffusion and language-model rows across Adult, Default, Shoppers, Magic and Beijing; SDMetrics supplies one metric among alpha-precision, beta-recall, attack AUC and machine-learning efficiency

title: TabKDE: Simple and Scalable Tabular Data Generation with Kernel Density Estimates
summary: Returns to classical tools for tabular generation: an ordinal-preserving encoding, a copula transform into the unit cube, and a kernel density estimate with covariance-aware directions and boundary-aware sampling, which needs almost no training, stores the model as a coreset of the original rows, and still matches diffusion-based methods on fidelity and leakage. SDV is the closest comparison and the paper runs three of its synthesizers directly, with the headline scalability claim measured against SDV's GaussianKDECopulaSynthesizer; CTGAN and TVAE also appear as baselines.
evidence: the introduction states that the Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016) includes generative modelling through low-rank modelling, GANs and vine-copula, achieving improved fidelity at heavy computational expense, which is the position TabKDE argues against; appendix B.2 lists CTGAN and TVAE (both Xu et al. 2019) among the baselines and the marginal and pairwise error tables carry their rows across Adult, Default, Shoppers, Magic, Beijing and News; appendix H.1 benchmarks against existing implementations in SDV, naming CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula and the GaussianKDECopulaSynthesizer implemented in SDV with default_distribution set to gaussian_kde, and reports it at 8,461 seconds on Adult against roughly one minute for TabKDE, which is the paper's scalability claim; the same table records the SDV copula models reaching near-ideal DCR at substantially higher error

title: Task-Conditioned Synthetic Data Generation for Improving Machine Learning Performance in Agricultural Prediction Tasks
summary: Reframes tabular synthesis for scarce agricultural reference data as a supervised problem rather than an unconditional mimicking one: a teacher model scores candidate rows for plausibility, informativeness and non-redundancy, and only samples that preserve the feature-target relationship survive, which is what separates useful augmentation from statistically realistic but task-misaligned samples. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six established generators run for comparison, taken from the Synthcity library, and both are reported as failing to deliver positive utility on crop-type classification or yield prediction.
evidence: the experimental section states that six established tabular SDG algorithms were drawn from the Synthcity Python library, naming Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks (CTGAN) (Xu et al. 2019) and Tabular Variational Autoencoders (TVAE) (Xu et al. 2019) alongside BN, ADSGAN, RTVAE and DDPM, selected for representative methodological coverage; the results report that CTGAN, ADSGAN, TVAE, RTVAE and DDPM did not provide significant positive utility in either task, and the win-rate table gives CTGAN 12 per cent merged and 2 per cent synthetic with negative win margins; the discussion groups CTGAN and TVAE below the real-data baseline for crop-type classification and notes their samples degrade further as the synthetic fraction grows

title: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement
summary: Addresses two failures at once for rare events in air transportation: generative models under-represent distributional tails, and they emit records that are individually plausible but operationally impossible, such as a short air time on a long route. A statistical layer extracts extremes by interquartile range to supply tail-focused training signal, and a learned anomaly-detection layer filters infeasible output afterwards. TVAE is the generative stage the framework is built around, and SDV's FixedCombinations constraint was tried for origin-destination consistency and rejected after it collapsed the distribution, replaced by the post-generation validity filter.
evidence: the introduction states that the dual-layer design brackets a Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) generative stage, chosen for training stability and lower computational cost than the alternatives, and section 2 later notes the generative component is model-agnostic so the TVAE could be replaced; the related-work section credits the Conditional Tabular GAN (Xu et al. 2019) and the Copula GAN (Patki et al. 2016) with introducing mode-specific conditional sampling and copula-based dependency modelling, and TVAE (Xu et al. 2019) as the tabular VAE adaptation; the data-preparation section describes the FixedCombinations constraint provided by the SDV library (Patki et al. 2016) as the established solution for encoding origin-destination pairs, then reports in Figure 6a that applying it caused distributional collapse by hiding airport-level structure from the model, so the authors kept the airport identifiers separate and replaced the constraint with their relational validity filter; the TVAE implementation source is not named
